comparator.name: Molecular Life Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 120 EC of named compulsory study, a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, a 21-EC bachelor thesis and 36 EC of open electives. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected by the official-order tie-break.
components: Introduction to Molecular Life Sciences and Biotechnology
Driving Forces in Chemistry, Physics and Biology
Responsibility and Reflection in Molecular Life Sciences
Selected by official-order tie-break from the 3-EC mathematics/statistics restricted choice.
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biophysical life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work, genetics, mathematics, programming and biomedical data.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible molecular-life-sciences response combining molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, laboratory research, mathematics and quantitative modelling.
progression: Life-science, programming, mathematics and laboratory foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease mechanisms and advanced quantitative analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Molecules, medicines & mechanisms of disease
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, infection, immunity, disease mechanisms and biomedical research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced medicines and molecular-disease direction through molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, pharmacology, infection, immunity, physiology and research methods.
progression: Biology, chemistry-related biochemistry, physiology, statistics and laboratory foundations precede molecular pathology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and medical applications. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes medicines, pharmacology, infection, immunity and molecular mechanisms of disease the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by five courses and 37.5 EC.

core: Molecular and cell biology, genetics and cellular processes
Biochemistry, proteins, metabolism and molecular mechanisms of health and disease
Chemistry, physics, thermodynamics, spectroscopy and biomolecular structure
Mathematics, modelling, bioinformatics, programming and data analysis
Laboratory research, experimental design, research ethics and independent thesis work
adjacent: Molecular medicines and mechanisms of disease
questions: How do molecules, proteins and cells interact to produce life and disease?
How can laboratory, mathematical and computational methods explain molecular systems?
How can molecular knowledge support medicines, diagnostics and sustainable innovation?

candidates.label: Molecular materials & sustainable technology
candidates.reason: UCR lacks the chemistry, physics, synthesis, nanotechnology and materials-science sequence needed to construct a coherent 24-course molecular-materials programme. Isolated environmental or modelling courses would not make that direction defensible.

selection.assessment: The closest molecular/cellular programme and a distinct medicines/disease programme are coherent and mechanically feasible. A third evidence-backed molecular-materials direction was tested but cannot be built as a coherent 24-course UCR curriculum because UCR lacks the necessary chemistry, physics, synthesis and materials-science sequence.

notes.text: WUR Molecular Life Sciences is a chemistry- and physics-intensive programme with general, organic, physical, bio-organic and bio-inorganic chemistry, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, spectroscopy, synthesis-oriented laboratory work and a 21-EC thesis. UCR offers substantial molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, biomedical science and quantitative analysis, but not a full molecular-life-sciences chemistry and physics sequence.
